source.title: Where's the Plan? Locating Latent Planning in Language Models with Lightweight Mechanistic Interventions

record.tranche_reason: Tests rhyme planning in open-weight models using linear probing, activation patching, and steering rather than the original studies' methods. It reports both decodability and whether interventions redirect rhyme generation.
record.gate_note: Rows record this study's probe, patching, and steering results. Cited results from prior work and the example completions are not recorded as study results. Probe-training choices and the Pile negative-control description are included only where the paper reports an outcome.
record.test_reason: The study uses linear probing and activation patching, with steering as a cross-check, to test whether open-weight models (Qwen3, Gemma-3, Llama-3, 0.6B–70B) represent the future rhyme before line 2. It also tests whether that representation causally drives generation. This bears directly on V2, V4 and V6. No frontier model is tested, so V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find encoding and causal use dissociable. Probes find newline rhyme information growing with scale in all three families, but only Gemma-3-27B uses it causally (handoff near layer 30, localized to five heads in layers 28/30). All other models condition on the rhyme word throughout. They conclude probe signal alone is not evidence of a planning site.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear probes and activation patching, with steering as a cross-check, rather than the methods of the cited original studies. The experiments focus on open-weight model families and rhyme-couplet completion.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family, model size, position (last word versus newline), and layer affect the result. The Gemma-3-27B handoff appears around layer 30; steering cross-checks the same model-dependent pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention versus MLP attribution: the Gemma-27B handoff is carried by five attention heads; MLP patches at the newline give 0% corrupt rhyme.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Where a newline planning site forms, it is routed by a sparse set of attention heads rather than MLPs.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The study covers three model families and one structured generation task. Patching uses 5 prompt pairs, and the authors note wide pair-to-pair variability and a wide upper bound on the recovered fraction. Probe results may reflect training-data distribution artifacts; rhyme matching uses a dictionary that may miss valid rhymes. The authors say further work is needed to distinguish genuine planning from effects that arise only when inserted by patching.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No frontier model is tested. Claude 3.5 Haiku results are only cited (Lindsey et al.).
The study does not test whether newline features are computed because they help later positions or arise as a side effect. It tests only encoding and causal use.
No tasks beyond rhyming couplets, and no chess, Sokoban or reasoning tasks.
Open attribution-graph or transcoder tools are not used. Only a single rhyming-couplet task is tested.

missing.what: Per-model peak per-layer patching rates (last word and newline), e.g. newline CI upper bound ≤0.21 for all models except Gemma-27B, and Llama newline upper bound ≤0.09
Comma-token (i=-1) patching in Gemma-27B is near zero, showing the handoff is specific to the newline token
Last-word patching in Gemma-27B drops sharply around layer 30 as newline patching rises (handoff crossover)

record.verdict_notes: Key correction: the reader treated last-word patching success as planning evidence. Last-word patching swaps the input rhyme cue r1 (fright→fear), and the authors read it as conditioning, not planning. Planning-site states must use the newline column, which is at noise for 12 of 13 models. V1 removed (no frontier model tested). V3 removed: the study does not test why features are computed, though unused newline encoding in most models is at least not evidence of pre-caching. Patching uses only 5 prompt pairs. The authors flag that the Gemma newline effect may appear only under artificial insertion.

versions.untested_parts: Tests rhyme planning in couplets across the named open-weight models, not rhyming verse generally or frontier models beyond those tested.
Tests linear decodability of the rhyme word from selected hidden states in couplet generation and general-text continuation; it does not test every token or task.
Tests causal use of newline representations in rhyme generation, but does not establish why the representations were computed or whether the mechanism generalizes beyond couplets.
Tests rhyme planning with probes and interventions in Qwen3, Gemma-3, and Llama-3; it does not use open attribution-graph tools.
No experiments on multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other tasks and architectures.
Tests rhyme-task decodability and causal use at the last-word and newline positions; does not identify a specific local heuristic or test look-ahead depth across other tasks.

rows.subject: Qwen3-32B
rows.operation_detail: Linear probes predict the rhyming token r2 from hidden states at the newline and other positions.

conditions.value: newline (i=0), compared with subsequent generated positions

rows.measure: Probe accuracy for predicting r2; the paper reports top-5, rhyme, and top-1 accuracy measures.
rows.baseline: Probes at subsequent generated positions (i>0); exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Newline and last-word probes substantially outperform probes at subsequent generated positions; exact values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: Wilson 95% CIs; exact intervals not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper states that peak-layer confidence bands do not overlap those for i≥1.
rows.check: Probes show decodability only, not a plan that steers generation, so V6 is not measured here. The paper itself finds no causal newline use in this model.

source_check.correct: V2: observed. V4: cannot_determine from probing alone; separate causal experiments find no newline use.
source_check.problem: The observed state is justified for decodability, not for V4's causal mechanism.

conditions.value: The Pile; 1,200 sampled sequences (1,000 train, 200 validation)

rows.subject: Gemma-3 family
rows.operation_detail: Compared the maximum across layers of the accuracy gap between newline and first-generated-position probes.
rows.measure: Maximum newline-versus-first-generated-position probe accuracy gap across layers.
rows.value: The positive gap rises from 0.11 at 1B to 0.38 at 27B; the paper reports a positive gap at every scale.
rows.uncertainty: 95% CIs; exact intervals not stated in text.
rows.note: Family-level trend reported by the authors; the stated endpoint values are not separate per-layer accuracies.
rows.check: The measure is the newline-minus-first-generated-position accuracy gap, which is relative concentration rather than decodability, so it does not bear on V2.

source_check.correct: V4: cannot_determine from this probing measure alone. The observed gap establishes concentrated rhyme information, not causal use.
source_check.problem: Observed conflates a planning-compatible representation with V4's causal planning mechanism.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-27B
rows.operation_detail: Simultaneously patched top-k attention-head outputs at the newline using corrupt-run outputs.

conditions.value: Top-k by attention to the last word

rows.baseline: Full-residual reference at best single layer: 63%.
rows.uncertainty: 95% cluster-bootstrap CIs are shown in Figure 7b; exact interval not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper says k=1, 2, and 3 yield near-zero rates and the effect plateaus through k=10.
rows.check: This is mechanism localization within Gemma-27B. Drop V1 and V3.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-27B

rows.check: Drop V1 and V3. The authors note the recovered-fraction CI extends past 1.0.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical row values match. States need version-specific treatment; probe-only rows cannot establish V4's causal mechanism. The authors' encoding-versus-use conclusion is accurately summarized; natural readout and generalization beyond the couplet task remain limitations.

statements.correction: Section 3.1: probes trained at various look-ahead distances k; accuracy decreases monotonically with k; k=8 overlaps unigram baseline. Figure 1's other exact offsets are not recoverable from this text.
statements.problem: The paper does not test general text only at k=8; the claimed untested interval is therefore unsupported.

statements.correction: Figure 3: last-word and newline probes both outperform subsequent generated-position probes; last-word probes peak earlier and decay later.
statements.problem: Newline versus last word is not a probe success-versus-failure contrast; both positions perform well.

statements.correction: Table 3 all-layer rates: Wilson 95% CIs. Figure 6b single-layer peak and Figures 7–8 head-patching rates: 95% cluster-bootstrap CIs over five prompt pairs.
statements.problem: The uncertainty description groups single-layer and head-patching results under Wilson intervals.

statements.correction: Single rhyming-couplet task. Patching: five prompt pairs, 20 samples per pair. Steering: ten schemes, 100 training prompts per scheme, 20 held-out prompts per scheme pair.
statements.problem: Five prompt pairs describes primary patching experiments, not all causal tests; steering uses a larger prompt set.

statements.correction: Section 3.1 and Figure 1: the k=8 probe-accuracy Wilson 95% band overlaps the unigram baseline across all layers in all three models.
statements.problem: The Wilson confidence band belongs to probe accuracy, not to the unigram baseline.

statements.correction: Last-word patching substitutes corrupt-rhyme-word activations; authors interpret most models as conditioning on that word throughout generation. A specific local heuristic is not isolated.
statements.problem: Input-cue swapping describes the intervention and its interpretation, not an independently established heuristic mechanism.

statements.correction: Gemma-3-27B: newline interventions change the final rhyme family; all-layer patching 67%, single-layer peak 0.63 at layer 33, steering 0.85–0.95. No separate intermediate-token regeneration test is reported.
statements.problem: The phrasing attributes an intermediate-token steering result to this study, whose reported outcome is the final rhyme-family rate.
